sections.title: Definition & Surgical Principles
sections.content: Evisceration involves removing intraocular contents while preserving the scleral shell, extraocular muscles, and optic nerve. Enucleation involves removal of the entire globe. The 'prosthetic shell' serves to restore volume and mimic natural appearance. Clinical goal: Maintain a healthy, well-formed conjunctival sac capable of retaining a customized ocular prosthesis.

sections.title: Socket Evaluation Components
content: Superior and inferior fornix depth (crucial for prosthesis retention)
Conjunctival health (look for discharge, keratinization, or chronic inflammation)
Volume assessment (check for superior sulcus deformity)
Implant motility (assessing the coupling between the orbital implant and the prosthesis)
Palpebral fissure width and eyelid position (ptosis vs. retraction)

sections.title: Prosthesis Maintenance Protocol
content: Step 1: Annual polish by Ocularist to remove biofilm and surface scratches.
Step 2: Daily cleaning with mild, non-abrasive soap and warm water.
Step 3: Lubrication with preservative-free artificial tears if dry eye symptoms persist.
Step 4: Periodic socket irrigation if mucopurulent discharge is noted.
Step 5: Replace prosthesis every 5-7 years to account for volume loss in the orbit.

sections.title: Red Flags (Emergency Signs)
content: Signs of orbital cellulitis (fever, erythema, extreme pain)
Sudden inability to retain the prosthesis
New onset socket mass/suspicion of recurrence (in cases of melanoma/R-B)

content.explanation: Socket (regular assessment), Surface (polish for smooth finish), Size (adjust for volume loss), Sanitation (daily cleaning).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always evaluate the socket without the prosthesis to grade baseline conjunctival health.
GPC in anophthalmic sockets is frequently caused by biofilm buildup on the prosthesis surface.
Use of a silicone sphere implant in evisceration provides better motility than simple scleral closure.
Secondary implants or dermis-fat grafts are gold standards for correcting post-enucleation volume deficits.
